findings.issue: The hero photo (general-hero-1) still has its own lettering printed into it ('Swim for Sunlit Days', a subline, and 'Shop Swimwear' / 'Explore the Collection' buttons), which shows through behind our H1, lead and button. The hero reads as two layers of overlapping text with dead buttons.
findings.reference: The competitor's hero photo is a clean shot with no lettering; the only text on it is the live eyebrow, title, lead and two buttons.
findings.fix: Give /custom-swimwear-printing/ a hero photo with no lettering, and take general-hero-1 out of the photo pool (other routes use it too) until it is regenerated without the text.

findings.issue: Each FAQ question is set smaller than its own answer: about 15px bold against about 17px body, at both widths. This is because reference.css sets `.block--faq { --size-subheading: 0.9375rem; }`, a fit variable that no site rule may set.
findings.reference: The competitor's questions ('Do I need a tech pack?') are bold and clearly larger than the smaller grey answer under them.
findings.fix: Remove the --size-subheading override on .block--faq (reference.css line 300) so the template sizes the question headings; keep the weight and colour on .faq__item h3.

findings.issue: On phones the H1, lead and button sit in the middle of the frame. Under the button there is an empty band about 140px tall of heavily darkened photo with no text on it.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone hero shows the face clear at the top and puts its eyebrow, title, lead and buttons at the bottom of the frame, ending just under the last button.
findings.fix: In reference.css at the phone breakpoint, align the .page-hero[data-variant="media-overlay"] content to the end of the frame (align-content / justify-content: end, with the normal bottom padding), so the copy sits at the bottom and the photo shows above it.

findings.issue: In the 2×2 phone grid the labels do not line up across a row. 'MINIMUM PER STYLE' is pushed to the bottom of its cell while 'BULK PRODUCTION TIME' starts higher, and under the one-line '300 dpi' there is a gap before its label.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps the parts of one row on a common line: their titles and texts start at the same height.
findings.fix: In reference.css, change `.trust-bar__item { align-content: space-between; }` (line 268) to align-content: start, so each value stacks directly over its label from the top of the cell.

findings.issue: The only thing in the left column is a one-line caption ('How a full-package swimwear project runs, from brief to delivery.') in small body text at the top. Beside the seven steps, the rest of that half is empty for about 600px.
findings.reference: The competitor's '3 Ways to Handover' left column carries the section's intro (eyebrow, heading, text, a 'Good to know' panel) and stays level with the numbered steps beside it.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set the .block--process intro caption as a lead (heading font, lead size) and make the intro column position: sticky (top offset under the header), so it stays in view beside the longer list.

findings.issue: On phones the wide-variant factory photo keeps its desktop strip ratio (about 2.3:1) and shrinks to a band about 150px tall under a long run of text, too small to read (this was reported before and has not changed).
findings.reference: The competitor's phone photos in text sections (the handover/mock-up image) run full width at a near-square or 4:3 ratio.
findings.fix: In reference.css at the stacked breakpoint, give the .block--split[data-variant="wide"] media aspect-ratio: 4 / 3 with object-fit: cover.

findings.issue: Two neighbouring sections of the same shape still stand one under the other: m7 'Mock-ups, Strike-offs and Sample Approval' and m8 'Print Lead Times, Pricing and Order Terms' both set their rows of short items as a list beside the heading.
findings.reference: Site rule: of two neighbouring sections made of short-item rows, the template sets only one of them as a list beside its heading.
findings.fix: When a process list and an iconList are neighbours, have the template give m8 the other iconList arrangement (items in columns under the heading).

findings.issue: On phones the fitted iconList item titles come out nearly as large as the section heading (about 26px against about 28px), and they break onto two lines ('Lower-cost / repeat printing', 'Higher-cost / print treatments'), so the item level is hardly below the heading and the titles do not keep to their lines. m3 ('Production / certifications') and m5 ('Placement / instead of repeat') show the same.
findings.reference: The competitor's item and card titles on phones ('Planning your collection', 'Custom Designs') are clearly a step below the section heading and hold one line.
findings.fix: In the template's heading fit, cap the h3 inside .block--icon-list on narrow widths at a step below the section's h2, and fit each title to keep to one line; no site rule sets the size.

findings.issue: After the photo band, m12 (proof), owner-testimonials and related all sit on white, so three neighbouring plain sections do not alternate. The earlier mint band is gone as asked and nothing should be put back on this one section, but the template's alternation does not give the testimonials or related section the tint.
findings.reference: The competitor alternates beige and white or navy bands from section to section; site rule: the template alternates white and --section-tint between neighbouring plain sections.
findings.fix: Include testimonials and relatedPages blocks in the template's white/tint alternation so the run reads white, tint, white.

findings.issue: The quote cards are white on the white band (--surface-testimonial: #ffffff), so their inner padding shows only as an unexplained 16–20px indent of every quote from the heading's left edge, at both widths.
findings.reference: Where the competitor insets card copy, the card is a visible panel (white 'Planning your collection' on beige, navy and aqua fills).
findings.fix: In reference.css, set --surface-testimonial to the page's tint (var(--surface-secondary)) so the cards read as panels like the featureGrid cards; otherwise drop the card's inline padding so the quotes start on the heading's edge.

findings.issue: The four related links are boxed in dark near-black 1px outlines, at both widths, so the row reads as a set of form fields.
findings.reference: The competitor's link rows ('Book a Call-Back', 'WhatsApp', 'Email Us') are filled white panels with no dark border; only the primary one is filled navy.
findings.fix: In reference.css, set the border of .related-links__link to a light var(--border-color) hairline (or none with a --surface-secondary fill).

findings.issue: On phones the comparison table still cuts its fourth column ('Pigment with white underlayer') off at the right edge, hinted only by a faint edge shadow, while the narrow first column sets 'White or pastel areas' one word per line.
findings.reference: On phones the competitor shows comparisons as stacked panels (the 'Plain colours' / 'Prints' cards), with nothing cut off sideways.
findings.fix: Give the prose comparison chart (.prose__chart[data-chart="comparison"]) a stacked phone layout, one card per column with its rows as label/value pairs, instead of the sideways scroll.

findings.issue: Even with the full-width rule (reference.css line 321), 'TALK TO US ABOUT CUSTOM PRINTING' still wraps to two lines in the pill, because the photo card's inner padding leaves the button only about 286px. The same label holds one line in the hero.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone buttons ('SEND US YOUR DESIGNS', 'TALK IT THROUGH FIRST') hold one line in a full-width pill.
findings.fix: At the phone breakpoint in reference.css, reduce the inline padding of [data-variant="image-band"] .cta / .cta__content to about 1.25rem and set .block--cta .cta .button to font-size 0.8125rem, so the label fits on one line.

findings.issue: The CTA heading 'Ready to Start Your Swimwear Print Project?' is set at line-height 1.4 (reference.css line 317), so its lines float apart at both widths, much looser than every other heading on the page (1–1.1).
findings.reference: The competitor's headings, including those on photos and dark bands, are set tight (about 1.1).
findings.fix: Remove `[data-variant="image-band"] .cta__heading { line-height: 1.4; }` or set it to 1.1, matching .block h2 and the hero h1.
